selfBuilt.title: Self-developed foundation
selfBuilt.intro: We keep critical parts of the large-model Token path under our own engineering lifecycle—ingress, metering, billing, and hand-off to upstream inference—so behavior stays predictable instead of stitched from unrelated components. This page expands the homepage card with the same title.

s1.title: Scope and boundaries
s1.body: In-house work focuses on platform-controlled scheduling, protocol alignment, observability, and commercialization; model intelligence still comes from compliant upstream engines. The model field in OpenAI-compatible calls selects SKUs we have onboarded and validated—see the console and model hub for capability limits.

s2.title: Token delivery and stability
s2.body: We normalize metering, streaming, and error semantics so switching models does not rewrite your client. Parameterize max_tokens, temperature, and similar knobs in production, and watch announcements for model lifecycle and multiplier changes.

s3.title: How this ties to API docs and the console
s3.body: The “First API call” doc covers auth, base_url, and samples; the console covers keys, usage, and invoices. The foundation does not change how you use OpenAI-style SDKs, but the gateway applies rate limits, auditing, and mapping—follow live responses and Swagger.

s4.title: Release cadence and compatibility
s4.body: Rollouts ship with in-app notices and doc updates. Plan canary windows and keep downgrade models for critical paths. Live capabilities and contracts are authoritative.

hardcore.title: Hardcore infrastructure
hardcore.intro: Owned compute and hardware clusters back throughput and latency at the physical layer: we shorten the path from “request hits the platform” to “capacity starts inferring,” and we keep redundancy and observability for peak traffic. This page expands the homepage card with the same title.

s1.title: Capacity and redundancy
s1.body: Capacity planning uses owned or long-term compute pools with headroom for typical peaks. Regions, redundancy, and SLA language belong in commercial agreements; ask about dedicated or isolated footprints through enterprise sales.

s2.title: Latency, geography, and routing
s2.body: With multiple ingress options, routing weighs client network health and upstream status to avoid congested or unnecessarily long paths. Prefer streaming/SSE for chat UX and handle cancellation cleanly.

s3.title: Peaks, queues, and scale-up
s3.body: Extreme peaks can still queue or return HTTP 429; implement backoff with bounded retries and keep downgrade paths. Higher concurrency, reserved capacity, or annual commits are usually negotiated commercially.

s4.title: Observability, triage, and support
s4.body: Retain request ids or traces when responses expose them to separate network, quota, and upstream issues. If latency or error rates spike, contact support with timeframe, model, and rough geography.

costPerf.title: Ultimate value
costPerf.intro: As an upstream Token supplier, we trim avoidable middle layers so more of your spend becomes actual usage: usage-based billing by default with clear dimensions for individuals and enterprises. This page expands the homepage card with the same title.

s1.title: Pricing logic and transparency
s1.body: Most SKUs price input and output tokens separately; long-context or high-multiplier models may use different unit rates. Treat console and hub pricing as authoritative—numbers here are illustrative.

s2.title: Statements, reconciliation, and plans
s2.body: The console exposes call history and billing filters as shipped—reconcile gateway usage against app logs on a cadence you trust. Bundles, prepaid balances, or promos follow their campaign pages and agreements.

s3.title: Enterprise procurement
s3.body: Where eligible, we support CNY settlement and corporate invoicing; tax treatment follows what sales confirms in writing. If web copy disagrees with your contract, the contract and pre-payment confirmation win.

s4.title: Channels and partners
s4.body: If you buy through a channel, still reconcile against platform statements and contracts. Partner onboarding rules live under “Partner program rules” in the sidebar; where pages disagree, follow the dedicated document.

privacy.title: Privacy first
privacy.intro: We default to necessity, minimization, and auditability for data related to API usage: TLS on the wire, access-controlled storage for sensitive configuration, and enterprise options for retention and compliance discussions.

s1.title: Transit and storage
s1.body: Clients talk to the gateway over HTTPS; persisted metadata for accounts, keys, and orders follows common access-control and auditing practices. Whether inference payloads are logged or retained—and for how long—depends on product mode and contract—confirm with legal/commercial before signing.

s2.title: Enterprise retention and compliance
s2.body: If regulations or internal policy require log geography, retention windows, or key rotation cadence, route through the enterprise evaluation path. We expose configuration or integrations where feasible, but you remain responsible as controller/processor with your counsel.

s3.title: API keys and separation of duties
s3.body: Use distinct keys per environment (dev/stage/prod) and rotate regularly; never ship long-lived secrets in public clients. Disable or revoke keys immediately on staffing changes—the console supports revocation.

s4.title: Disclaimers and updates
s4.body: This page is a product overview—not legal advice. Privacy notices and DPAs follow the published versions; when they change, we will announce them—keep contact channels current.

docsPartnerRules.title: Partner program rules
docsPartnerRules.intro: These rules apply to partners who apply through this platform to resell compute and model services. Final commercial terms are governed by signed agreements; this page is a public summary so you can review the basics before joining.

s1.title: 1. Scope and eligibility
s1.body: The program is for legally registered businesses or authorized team leads who can bear civil liability independently. You must provide truthful information; we may request additional documents during review or operations. If anything differs from the public /partners page, the information you confirm before payment and your contract prevail.

s2.title: 2. Fees and payment
s2.body: Fees are as published on the platform. Complete payment only through the official channels we provide and keep your receipts. Risks from unofficial payments are yours. Partner benefits and support start after payment is received and approval is granted.

s3.title: 3. Marketing and compliance
s3.body: You must describe product capabilities, pricing, and limits accurately—no false or misleading claims. You must follow applicable laws and regulations. You bear responsibility for complaints, penalties, or losses caused by non-compliant marketing. We may suspend or end the partnership depending on severity.

s4.title: 4. Support and disputes
s4.body: We may notify you of policy updates via announcements, email, or in-app messages—please keep contact details current. For questions on rules or settlements, use the Contact page. Disputes should first be resolved through good-faith negotiation; where negotiation fails, applicable law and your contract apply.
